_comment: What FormatDeparturesUseCase turns a prediction set into. Offsets rather
than absolute timestamps, because formatETA is relative to Clock.System.now()
— an absolute fixture would decay into a different expectation every day.
AndroidWidgetManager.formatForWidget is NOT the formatter. It returns a
hardcoded 'Loading...' placeholder and always has; the real formatting runs
in FormatDeparturesUseCase, called from DepartureWidgetProvider. Recorded
here so AV2-5.3 does not wire the widget to the placeholder by following

cases.name: ordering is by arrival time, not by the formatted string
cases.note: THE regression this pins. Sorting on the eta STRING orders lexicographically — '1 min' < '10 min' < '2 min' < 'Due' — and combined with take(3) the widget showed the wrong three trains in the wrong order.
cases._countNote: take(3). A fourth train is formatted and then dropped.

cases.name: station suffixes are stripped from the destination
a long destination is truncated at 22 plus an ellipsis
cases._rule: over 25 characters -> take(22) + '...'. Note the 22 is a raw character count with no word-boundary awareness, so a truncation can end mid-word or, as here, on a dangling ampersand. Recorded because it looks like a bug and is not one — it is what v1 shows today.

cases.name: a filter that matches nothing fails OPEN
cases.note: The widget has no empty state to explain itself with, so a filter matching nothing must show the unfiltered list rather than leave a silently blank widget.

cases.name: a blank destId is admitted by any filter
cases.note: TfL sends 'Check Front of Train' and depot moves that map to no station. A plain `in` test would drop them from the widget while the board still showed them.

carriedThrough.stationName: from the selection, not the payload
carriedThrough._statusNote: always null out of this use case; line status is applied later from the repository
